title: The Decision That Went Wrong
teaching_need: Learners often struggle to make a defensible institutional recommendation when evidence is incomplete, conflicting and consequential—mistaking early promising results for settled proof, overlooking stakeholder impacts, or treating uncertainty as a reason to avoid judgement.
intended_capability: Interpret conflicting quantitative and qualitative evidence in a developing institutional case, weigh stakeholder perspectives and trade-offs, and reach a justified recommendation under genuine uncertainty.
summary: A 90-minute Learning Journey set in a fictional UK university considering an AI-assisted student support system. Learners meet early pilot evidence, examine it more carefully, encounter later conflicting findings and stakeholder perspectives, then produce a committee recommendation that remains open to more than one defensible outcome.
primary_pattern: Evidence-informed decision-making under uncertainty through progressive disclosure of conflicting evidence
supporting_patterns: Critical interpretation of quantitative and qualitative evaluation findings
Attention to stakeholder perspectives and consequences
Reasoning under uncertainty with genuine ambiguity preserved
Justified recommendation with opportunity to reconsider earlier judgement
learning_sequence: Overview — orientation to the institutional case and expectations
The Promising Pilot (Interactive) — make sense of early evaluation evidence and form an initial case
Reading the Evidence Carefully (Expository) — examine what the figures and records can and cannot support
When the Evidence Changes (Interactive) — weigh later findings, benefits, concerns and reconsider earlier judgement
The People Behind the Decision (Interactive) — consider stakeholder consequences and what the evidence can support
The Committee Recommendation (Assessment Pack) — choose among options and justify a recommendation under uncertainty
transferable_principle: When there is no single unambiguously correct decision, develop judgement by revealing evidence progressively, distinguishing observation from interpretation, bringing stakeholder consequences into view, and requiring a justified recommendation that can survive new or conflicting information. The institutional AI scenario is the vehicle, not the transferable core.
